items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: But he’s in the home movies that Mona Hinton shot that I’ve used in my movies.

ctx.x: Well I found him, because I put an ad in the Amsterdam News which is a Harlem newspaper, with the photograph. See I loved all this part of producing the movie, tracking people down, loved that. And I said, “do you remember this photo?” I said, “it ran in Esquire” and I told the date and it was taken in the summer of ‘58. “Were you there? Do you know anyone who was? If so call this number.” And I had a separate telephone with © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -15-

an answering machine attached. And people started checking in. And one was the little boy sitting next to Basie. So that was nice. Basie sat down when everybody else was standing, because I think his legs gave out. And in later years of course he was in this wheelchair that he drove himself. It was kind of marvelous. But the other person that decided to sit down was Willie the Lion Smith. And he’s so big and pompous and arrogant you know. And he was standing there with this man who is half his size, Lucky Roberts…
